parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4's core step — existence of a tree component and the signed (bipartition) sum bound |Ξ| ≤ Σε_i + [M odd]a_M — is asserted as 'standard; details omitted'; this is exactly where the budget K ≤ n is used.

errors.description: The crux of the lower bound is not proved. One must count edges (⌊M/2⌋) versus vertices (n+1) to find an acyclic component, then 2-colour it to get the signs, so that unmatched parts and the ±ε_i telescoping give the bound. This is the only place where K ≤ n enters; without it the claim is false, so it cannot be dismissed as routine.
errors.quote: there is a set $V_T\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}$ and signs $s:V_T\to\{\pm1\}$ such that the signed sum $\Xi:=\sum_{j\in V_T}s(j)\,q_j$ satisfies $|\Xi|\le\sum_i\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted)

errors.description: Numerical/Monte-Carlo verification is repeatedly cited as support (for the answer, Lemma 4 and Lemma 5). These carry no proof value; the closing parenthetical could be mistaken for evidence in place of argument, though the write-up does not formally rely on it.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) is consistent with a hand check at n=1. Lemma 2 (picking-phase value), the reduction, the signed subset-sum property (3.1), and the full upper-bound construction in Lemma 5 (pigeonhole + cross-pairing cuts, mark count ≤ n) are correct and carefully written.
